newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to fine Colombian carrier for safety violation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to fine Colombian carrier for safety violation.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration says it has proposed fining Colombian all-cargo airline Aerovias Colombianas (ARCA) $68,000 for failure to install vents on the main cargo doors of its DC-8-55 freighters.
ARCA has 15 days to respond to the proposed fine, and the FAA could alter the penalty as part of a settlement with the carrier.
Failure to achieve a settlement would see the issue handed over to the U.S. District Court for prosecution.
The vents, which the airline had been required to install, are designed to prevent the accidental opening of the doors in flight.
The FAA alleges ARCA was in non-compliance on 686 flights from June 1992 through August 1993.
The FAA said that while ARCA was Colombian-registered, the carrier also flew U.S.-registered aircraft and was required to follow a U.S.-approved maintenance program.
Colombian authorities suspended ARCA's operating certificate on Jan 24. The grounding remains in effect, said the FAA.
In April, the FAA said it would fine the airline $79,000 for failure to follow required maintenance schedules.
